chapter: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
title: Richard M. Jones in New Orleans and his death
summary: How Jones met Richard M. Jones, his early-1930s band, his lawsuit over a song, the music he sent, and his death.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Mmhmm. But uh, did you know him up in Donaldsonville or?

No, no. I met him, when I met him, he had came here from Chicago. But uh, he had, he hadn't been gone long when I came to New Orleans and that was around 1925. His wife was, his wife was still living around here. Right down there by that church. Everybody know where Nat Dahl lived? Right across the street. His wife was some kind of- Is that Liberty? Yeah. Richard M. Jones's wife was a singer, some kind of, some kind of classical singer, something like that. Do you know her name? No, I don't know, I don't know, I don't know, I don't know. I remember seeing her, but I don't know.
You don't remember her name. You must have known her a little bit. Richard M. Jones came back to New Orleans for, just for a visit. You mean?

Who? Yeah, he only came here. No, he came here instead. Look, he came here and stayed here. And when I saw him, he had formed the band around here, right here. That was around in the early 30s. And he had Didi. You asked Didi about it. Didi was playing with him. I never knew that. Didi was playing with him. Yeah? Who else was in the band? I forgot. But I saw him, I went up, I didn't go to nothing but dances and I saw them up at the, saw him up at the Bulls. We call it the Bulls, it's the Elks now. Yeah. But that used to be the Bulls. Yeah. Oh, he played up there? Richard M. Jones. Yeah. And then he left again to Chicago. Left, went back to Chicago. That's when he died. But before he died, he had sent me some music, L-Ray wagon and all something else. Then he had a suit dent against this man that wrote, shoot, shoot, shoot, baby, because he was claiming it. You know, he used to copy that letter. And right after that, my daddy told me that Richard M. Jones, we call him Manny. He had some sardines. He had been drinking. He got two men for it and died.
Well, fish will go bad in a hurry. Hmm? Say fish will go bad in a hurry, I guess. Do you see my cousin?
Which one? Lionel, his son, Lionel. He got a son here. He's a drummer.
Lionel Jones? Sure. I never met him. How did Richard M. Jones get that nickname?

I don't know. Money. That's all I know. Money. My grandma and all call her money. Richard M. Jones' son, he should be in one of those books I got here. Yeah. He was in the union. Well, how was his leg then? I don't know. He had a stiff leg. Yeah, he had a stiff leg. He dragged that leg. Yeah. But he was bigger than I was. He used to sing too, you know. Mm-hmm. But I wouldn't sing. Do you have any of his music that he sent you? I can't find it. No, I was trying to look for some stuff before you all can. Yeah. See, I've been sick and be upset at this house. My wife came in and cleaned up. But I had a little ring wagon. That does it. And something around. I said, that does it when they clean up. Yeah.
Yeah. You still have some of those old things flying around here somewhere?
Yeah, he used to send me piano copies. Yeah. Yeah, I love to see those things.
